_comment: Tracked deprecations awaiting removal. The deprecation-reaper workflow reads this file weekly, looks up when each entry's PR merged (its exact mergedAt timestamp), and once mergedAt + grace has elapsed it opens/refreshes a tracking issue and pings the owners. Entries whose PR is not merged yet are ignored, so the clock only starts at merge. Remove an entry once its functions are deleted.

deprecations.description: The Runtime API entry points that identify a command queue by raw id are deprecated in favor of overloads taking MeshCommandQueue& (tt-metal#51559): BeginTraceCapture(MeshDevice*, uint8_t) -> MeshDevice::begin_mesh_trace(MeshCommandQueue&), Synchronize(MeshDevice*, std::optional<uint8_t>, ...) -> Synchronize(MeshDevice&, ttsl::optional_reference<MeshCommandQueue>, ...), MeshDevice::{begin,end,replay}_mesh_trace(uint8_t, ...) -> the same members taking MeshCommandQueue&, and MeshEvent(uint32_t, MeshDevice*, uint32_t, const MeshCoordinateRange&) -> MeshEvent(uint32_t, MeshCommandQueue&, const MeshCoordinateRange&). All in-repo call sites are already migrated; the id-based overloads remain only for external callers during the grace period. The cleanup PR deletes them and their definitions in distributed.cpp, mesh_device.cpp and mesh_event.cpp, leaving only the MeshCommandQueue& forms.

IDevice::sysmem_manager() is deprecated (tt-metal#64081): SystemMemoryManager was removed, and host command queues (HostCq, CqBacking) are internal to tt_metal with no public replacement. The deprecated pure virtual stays so that out-of-tree IDevice subclasses and callers still compile; every in-repo override throws. The cleanup PR deletes the declaration from device.hpp and mesh_device.hpp, the SystemMemoryManager forward declarations, and the throwing overrides in device.cpp and mesh_device.cpp.
